summary: Ground-level fire lookout site in Blaine County, Montana, now gone. A video says its building burned in the 1980s; the buttes lie on the Fort Belknap Reservation.

facts.design: Ground structure, not a tower (per the FFLA type column)
facts.status_note: The FFLA lists the lookout as gone, and a video title says its building burned in the 1980s. No source read says what remains on the summit.

visit.trail_note: A 2021 hiking blog climbed Middle Butte, the tallest of the Three Buttes; it names no trailhead or route.

events.note: The video title gives only the decade (the 1980s); 1980 is entered as a stand-in for that decade.

notes_for_editor: Thin evidence. The lookout-specific facts come only from two YouTube titles (the video pages were read as titles, not descriptions) and one 2021 hiking blog. No agency, heritage-register, newspaper or photo source was found, so builder, design and date are unknown. The 1930s date is a title's 'possibly' and is kept out of facts and events. Access is left unset: the buttes are on the Fort Belknap Reservation, and no source read states the access rule or whether permission is needed; a human should check with the tribe or the managing body before publishing an access level. The 'tribal land' gloss was removed from the story on 2026-10-21 because no source read supports it. Name collision: a cached Siuslaw National Forest page (Oregon) mentions a different 'Three Buttes' lookout with a 1934 new lookout, which is not this site. Leads not read: a Rod Benson Instagram reel (Jan 2024) and a Facebook post describe the old lookout cabin as having burned, and a 1988 tDAR record, 'Three Buttes East Road Project, Fort Belknap Reservation' (Marvin Keller), may be a cultural survey.
